text: In nineteen eighty-three, a brand-new Air Canada jet ran out of fuel at forty-one thousand feet. Canada was switching to metric. The fuel was worked out in pounds instead of kilograms. The jet had less than half of what it needed. Halfway to Edmonton, both engines stopped. Most of the screens went dark. A tiny propeller dropped out of the belly to keep the controls alive. The captain was a glider pilot. He aimed for Gimli, an old air force base. It was now a race track, and it was race day. He slipped the jet down sideways, the nose wheel collapsed, and it scraped to a stop. Nobody was seriously hurt. Dave was waving the chequered flag.
